top_choice_rationale: P004 (Kiyotaki and Moore) rests on one originating 1997 paper, so the two-name credit set matches the discovery exactly. Its contribution is a disciplined mechanism in which collateral constraints with endogenous asset prices turn small shocks into persistent credit cycles, and it has had almost three decades of extension and criticism. It is a close call over P001. Direct identification of the aggregate amplification multiplier is weaker than the firm-level evidence for Melitz-Helpman selection and reallocation. The firm-level collateral channel does have support, and the citation should rest on the mechanism and not claim a measured multiplier. The overlap with the 2022 prize looks thematic and not a duplicate of the discovery. P001 is a very close second because its mechanism is mature, directly tested on microdata and distinct from the 2008 trade prize, though Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum remain an attribution concern. P002 is scientifically major, but a three-name set cannot settle its dispersed credit and the micro evidence on Calvo pricing is mixed. P003 is high-quality evidence, but its boundary between the task framework and the China-shock work is unresolved. A credible, defensible prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No tie to Kiyotaki, Moore or the other credited names on P001, P002 or P003 is apparent from the profile. Disclosures: my corporate finance and financial contracting field is adjacent to the enforcement friction behind P004. I am listed among the KVA experts for the 2022 prize, so I may misjudge its overlap with P004. I hold an adjunct post at Chicago Booth, share an SSE affiliation with other members, and have long committee overlap with Hassler and Krusell. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
